name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Betty McCollum is a well-funded incumbent with no outside opposition spending
Republican challenger has raised only about $28,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price McCollum at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: McCollum holds a seat that leans Democratic by 18 points, has a large fundraising advantage, and faces an underfunded challenger with no outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against McCollum or a major scandal would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Betty McCollum is seeking another term in a St. Paul-area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. She has raised about $1.25 million and holds nearly $500,000 on hand, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised under $30,000 and reports only about $2,200 in cash. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and no independent polls of the race are available.

With no expert ratings published, the picture rests on fundamentals, money, and markets, all of which favor McCollum heavily. Prediction markets put her chances around 96 percent, and the expected margin is roughly 24 points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
